Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Football The beacon of hope: Coach Opeele touts Andre Ayew as the man to rescue Ghana football 17 November 2026 5:45am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
A growing call for change at the top of Ghana football is gaining momentum, with former Black Stars captain Andre "Dede" Ayew emerging as the people's favourite to lead the Ghana Football Association (GFA) into a new era.
In a Facebook post, football coach Isaac Opeele - who openly declares his affiliation with GFA President Kurt Okraku - has described Dede Ayew as the "beacon of hope" for Ghana football, arguing that the growing public clamour for the former national campyain to contest the GFA presidency, is not about hatred for the current leadership, but about a desire for change, following what he says many believe are the ills of the current administration.
Kurt Okraku is in the final and 8th year of his second term as GFA President, and despite the GFA's controversial move to amend its constitution in the middle of Kurt's final term to enable him run for a third term, Ghanaians and some football stakeholders have said Ghana football has deteriorated under the leadership of Kurt so he must bow out at the end of his term in the interest of Ghana football.
And according to Opeele, the pioneer argument for change is not personal.
"The pioneer argument and reason the Ghanaian public want a change at the GFA is not because they hate Kurt Okraku but they think the association is overly corrupt; they think the GFA has ceased to care about the feeling of the masses; they think the GFA leadership is incompetent," Coach Opeele wrote on Facebook.
These reasons, Opeele added, is why Ghanaians and some football stakeholders have gladly welcomed the rumour of Dede Ayew's GFA presidential ambition - as they they see him as the vehicle to drive change.
"Ghanaians just want Kurt Okraku to go. It is they gladly welcomed the rumour of Dede Ayew's GFA presidential ambition. They see Dede as the kind of vehicle or a strong force to drive into the fray to unseat Kurt Okraku," he added.
With the front of football stakeholders said to have been sharply divided in the past seven years, Opeele described Dede as a unifier, likening him to ''that palatable central in a movie that can unite factions within the GFA to recreate the Black Stars' victorious glorious days. "
Coach Opeele touted many positives he argued are leadership qualities Andre Ayew possesses.
First, he compared Dede's leadership character to that of Cameroon's Samuel Eto'o, who moved from the pitch to lead his country's football federation, before highlighting other strengths he stressed wi help Ghana football.
"Dede Ayew has that strong vibrant character like Cameroon's Samuel Eto'o. He is bilingual i.e dealing French speaking countries in Africa. He is a famous international brand he appeals to the Gen Z's and he has an unmatched charisma," Coach Opeele continued.
As the son of the influential Abedi Pele, Coach Opeele argued that Dede inherits a legendary status that will open doors for Ghana in the oil-rich Arab nations, Europe and at FIFA.
As the conversation grows, Opeele noted that Dede has been smart - keeping mute over his interest directly, but continuing to show up at major football events
"He has been smart and indirectly kept mute over his interest but keeps showing up at events to get under the skin of Kurt Okraku," Opeele noted, observing that the quiet presence has only fuelled the public rallying call.
Publicly, the former Black Stars captain has attracted support from key figures across all walks of life.
Among them is veteran broadcaster Kwame Sefa Kayi of Peace FM, who publicly backed Dede to seize the opportunity, a backing Opeele says referenced in his article.
Also, Andre Ayews support is said to be growing among football stakeholders, with many of them admiring Ayew's courage to show up and rescue the game, rather than opting for the easy option of taking an appointment with the current administration.
Concluding, Coach Opeele observed that both the public and the media have lost confidence in the GFA leadership, having sold it out as as "one with zero credibility, arrogant, ineffective and a predacious leader with no achievement."
"Indeed, the Kurt Okraku's brand, that am part of, is becoming the biggest loser, he noted.
Coach Opeele slammed the GFA President's 'present inner circle for ''telling him what he wants to hear," which he said ''is slowly killing Ghana football of which the public cannot afford to see it decompose hence the public rallying call on Dede Ayew."
